data.title: Leopalace21 Backs HIKARI TSUSHIN-Led Tender Offer and Plans Subsidiary Restructuring
data.description:
The latest announcement is out from Leopalace21 ( (JP:8848) ).

Leopalace21’s board has endorsed a tender offer by K891, Inc., a HIKARI TSUSHIN-affiliated vehicle, to acquire all common shares and certain stock acquisition rights, with the aim of turning Leopalace21 into a wholly owned subsidiary and subsequently delisting its shares. The board is recommending that shareholders and stock option holders tender their holdings into the offer, which runs from September 15 to October 30, 2026, at a purchase price of ¥1,000 per share of common stock.

As part of the transaction structure, Leopalace21 will reclassify all shares of its specified subsidiary ASUKA SSI into voting and non-voting classes and transfer a portion of the voting shares to THE INSURANT GROUP, a consolidated subsidiary of HIKARI TSUSHIN. This share transfer will result in a change in Leopalace21’s specified subsidiary status, signalling a broader reorganization of the group under HIKARI TSUSHIN’s control and reshaping governance and ownership for existing stakeholders.

data.title: Nickel Industries weathers Sulawesi drought as Excelsior ramp‑up slows but Hengjaya mine hits record sales
data.description:
The latest update is out from Nickel Mines Ltd. ( (AU:NIC) ).

Nickel Industries has reported that commissioning of its Excelsior Nickel Cobalt HPAL project in Central Sulawesi has been temporarily constrained by unusually dry conditions that have sharply reduced water availability, forcing operations to run at about 30% of nameplate capacity until the expected onset of the wet season later this year. Despite the weather‑related setback, the company noted that its rotary kiln electric furnace operations remain unaffected and that Excelsior had reached roughly 50% capacity within four weeks of commissioning before the drought‑driven slowdown.

Regulatory progress has offset some of the operational headwinds, with the company securing an exemption to Indonesia’s restrictions on mixed hydroxide precipitate exports and advancing toward an industrial business licence that will permit commercial sales of Excelsior’s full suite of nickel and cobalt products. At the same time, the Hengjaya Mine has capitalised on the dry conditions to deliver record monthly nickel ore sales and strong EBITDA, helping lift combined adjusted EBITDA from existing operations to about US$90 million over July and August and prompting an application to increase its annual sales quota.

data.title: ArborGen Shifts From Expansion to Cash Generation as CEO Exits and Shareholders Press for Value
data.description:
ArborGen Holdings ( (NZ:ARB) ) just unveiled an update.

ArborGen told shareholders its performance and share-price remain below expectations, despite record revenue in FY26 and an improving earnings margin driven by a strategic shift toward higher-value seedling products. Management highlighted Brazil as a fast-growing but operationally demanding market, and the U.S. South as a mature business undergoing cost-cutting and footprint rationalisation amid weaker housing, lower timber harvesting and declining pulp demand.

The board signalled a clear pivot from heavy growth investment to cash generation and debt reduction, including disciplined capex, working-capital tightening and selective asset sales such as the Ridgeville building. It acknowledged shareholder frustration over liquidity and valuation, but stopped short of launching a new formal strategic review, instead committing to ongoing portfolio assessment, stronger execution in both regions and tighter alignment of executive pay with long-term shareholder returns.

data.title: Mandrake Advances Utah Lithium Project With Bulk Brine Testing
data.description:
An announcement from Mandrake Resources Ltd ( (AU:MAN) ) is now available.

Mandrake Resources has completed swabbing operations at the Evelyn Chambers #1 well in Utah, recovering about 8,000 litres of lithium brine from existing perforations in the Leadville Formation, which were originally designed for now-depleted oil and gas production. The extracted brine has been transported to U.S.-based Direct Lithium Extraction provider Electroflow Technologies Inc and other DLE groups for technical and commercial testing.

Electroflow plans to process Mandrake’s brine into battery-grade lithium carbonate and lithium iron phosphate, with the appraisal to yield key data on purity, recovery and costs that will underpin future scoping studies for the project. The bulk brine program was largely funded through a US$1 million grant from the U.S. Department of Energy to the Paradox Basin Lithium Group, reducing Mandrake’s costs while advancing the company’s positioning in the emerging U.S. lithium supply chain.
